source_row.rationale: ACOG describes placenta previa as a cause of later-pregnancy vaginal bleeding that often occurs without pain. Placental abruption more often includes abdominal or back pain. Intact membranes and a reassuring fetal tracing make vasa previa less consistent with the complete presentation, though any third-trimester bleeding requires urgent obstetric evaluation.
source_row.source_detail: ACOG Bleeding During Pregnancy — placental causes later in pregnancy: placental abruption commonly includes abdominal/back pain; placenta previa bleeding often occurs without pain. source_row.stem: A pregnant client at 34 weeks with intact membranes develops sudden painless bright-red vaginal bleeding. The fetal heart tracing is reassuring. Which condition is most consistent with this presentation?
